translations.answer: The maintainer provides a single clear interface: the first parameter of the 'wrench cone constructor' defines the rotation. The thread does not provide information about the rotation matrix direction, reference frame convention, or re-validation code, so it can only be used as an entry point for localization, and cannot be directly used to construct the matrix from a picture alone.
translations.applicability: This applies to the thread period of the Crocoddyl wrench cone constructor; the parameter types, rotation direction, and frame convention must be verified by checking the source code or documentation in the current version.
translations.credibility.rationale: No reproducible records have been formed.
translations.details.attempts.0: The author checked the contact wrench cone paper and asked the maintainer if it also covers friction, ZMP/CoP, and yaw torque.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author provided an image of two feet not aligned with the world coordinate system and asked for the rotation matrix.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: The contact model requires separate checks for tangential friction, CoP support domain, and yaw torque boundary, rather than just seeing a friction cone and assuming full foot stability.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: The rotation parameter used in the wrench cone constructor must be verified and aligned with the actual foot direction.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: A complete finite foot constraint requires using the contact wrench cone, and the friction cone or CoP cost should be removed to avoid duplication.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: When the foot is not aligned with the world frame, the first parameter of the wrench cone constructor should be used to specify the rotation.
translations.details.environments.0: Crocoddyl whole-body manipulation example, thread time from 2020-10 to 2021-02; no Crocoddyl version or robot model provided.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread does not provide specific API version, matrix direction, or code example for the contact wrench cone.
translations.details.limits.1: It is not possible to derive the rotation matrix from a foot image alone; one must return to the target version and reference frame definition to construct the function.
translations.details.limits.2: This discussion is from 2020/2021; the current Crocoddyl API name needs to be verified again.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The author responded with clarification and stated they will update the example after the scheme is implemented; no further implementation or numerical results were provided.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The rotation parameter issue is only mentioned by the maintainer in the interface, without any author verification.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Is the friction cone or CoP/ZMP cost sufficient for whole-body manipulation? When should the contact wrench cone be used instead?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How should the wrench cone be oriented when the feet are not aligned with the world frame?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: In high dynamic real-world operations, both friction margin and CoP support domain should be monitored, and errors in the reference frame could result in seemingly feasible but unexecutable contact force moments.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The example was written before the contact wrench cone function was developed; the maintainer explained this is the example and it still uses the friction cone, not indicating that it is sufficient.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The user cannot determine the relationship between the friction cone, CoP/ZMP cost, and the contact wrench cone in high dynamic whole-body operations.
translations.details.symptoms.1: When the foot has a yaw angle, the user is unclear on how the wrench cone rotation matrix is defined.
translations.media_summaries.0: Comment 722446675's image has been verified: the left side is a photo of the footplate, and the right side shows a diagram with Left foot, Right foot, support polygon, support polygon with margin, and Δx_zmp. The feet are not parallel; the image supports the question 'Are the feet not aligned with the same world frame?', but lacks coordinate axes or matrix definition, so it cannot be used to derive the rotation parameters.
translations.source.locator: Crocoddyl #880: Author comment 722446675 provides footplate image and asks the question; maintainer comment 771044606 points out that the first parameter of the constructor defines the rotation.
translations.source.title: Configuration of contact wrench cone in Crocoddyl whole-body manipulation with foot rotation
translations.terms.3: Contact wrench cone (contact wrench cone) (接触力矩锥)
translations.title: How is the rotation of the contact wrench cone specified when the feet are not aligned with the world frame in Crocoddyl?
